text:
opsbot: :rotating_light: Alert: routing-service detected increased error rate for model-serving with unexpected variant mismatch at 1975009876
opsbot: Metric: 502s spiking on /v1/generate, anomaly score 8.7, impacted region eu-west-1 and us-east-1
pagerduty: Paging @oncall-sre -> primary: irene, secondary: sanjay :telephone_receiver:
irene: I'm on it, grabbing context and runbook. Who owns smart-routing policy config? :eyes:
aisha: I manage the routing-policy service (aisha). Noticed a small rollout earlier for per-tenant variant overrides at 1975009400 — may be related.
kevin: Observed unusual KV hit patterns: shard-12 has keys with mixed model ids and region prefixes. Looks like prefix generation changed in last deploy.
marta: Confirming — config commit 7f3a2b added a normalization step that accidentally drops model:region delimiter for some legacy workloads.
irene: That could cause cache key collisions where variant A from eu gets served to requests pinned to variant B in us. Are we seeing cross-tenant misserve?
kevin: Initial trace: request id r-0a3f -> expected variant: gpt-3k-opt, served variant: gpt-7k-lr. KV lookup returned entry for key 'gpt7k_eu-shard12' but request key computed as 'gpt7k_eu-shard12' (delimiter collapsed).
sanjay: That's exactly the pattern. Smart-routing fallback logic uses KV prefix to reuse prefix caches. If delimiter missing, KV names collide across variants.
aisha: Immediate mitigation proposal: revert the normalization commit or disable prefix-based reuse in routing-service in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. Which is faster?
kevin: Disabling prefix reuse is a config flip, faster. Revert requires deploy.
irene: Do it. Flip config and flush affected shards. I'll take pager and coordinate.
opsbot: runbook link: https://confluence.redwood/incident/runbooks/kv-prefix-mismatch
opsbot: Executing change: set routing-service.disable_prefix_reuse=true on eu-west-1,us-east-1 (dry-run 1s)
kevin: Pushing config now: 
```
# envoy config patch
PATCH /configs/routing-service
set disable_prefix_reuse = true
```
kevin: Config push initiated to eu-west-1,us-east-1 — rolling update will be done by 1975009925
aisha: While we flip, we should flush KV caches on shards 11-14. Command: `kvctl flush --shard 11,12,13,14 --pattern "gpt*"`
marta: I'll run the flush on eu-west-1 now.
marta: ```
> kvctl flush --shard 12 --pattern "gpt*"
Flushed 12,345 keys from shard-12
> kvctl flush --shard 11,13,14 --pattern "gpt*"
Flushed 3,210 keys from shard-11, 2,902 keys from shard-13, 1,004 keys from shard-14
```
irene: Config flip is in, cache flush completed. Monitoring for error rate drop.
kevin: Early signs: 502s dropped ~60% in eu-west-1, ~45% in us-east-1 at 1975009940. Continued watch.
support-bot: Notifying support queues: support-team@redwood; will prepare customer impact list.
aisha: Customer impact check: which tenants hit variant misserve? We have tracing info for request ids. I'm compiling list.
aisha: Preliminary affected customers: [AcmeCorp (heavy traffic), LibratoAI (low traffic), PixelPay (high priority enterprise)], impact: intermittent wrong model outputs, sometimes longer latency.
sanjay: Severity classification: P1 for AcmeCorp (high error rate, transactions affected), P2 for PixelPay, P3 for others. Recommend outbound comms to AcmeCorp immediately.
irene: I'll draft a short status for status.redwood.com and send SRE -> CSM heads for a coordinated message. Keep thread for live updates.
kevin: Root cause: normalization step removed the ':' delimiter in some key paths when tenant had legacy model alias. That produced keys like 'gpt7k_eu' instead of 'gpt:7k_eu', causing collisions between 'gpt7k' and 'gpt:7k'.
aisha: Remediation plan: 1) keep disable_prefix_reuse until we release a proper fix, 2) revert normalization in next deploy with tests, 3) backfill KV to safe names and add linting to prevent delimiter loss.
marta: I've opened PR #4621 to revert and add unit tests. Marking for expedited review.
opsbot: Incident timeline updated in PagerDuty (INC1975009876).
pagerduty: Reminder: schedule handoff at +30m. Primary irene -> secondary sanjay if not resolved.
irene: Handing to sanjay at 1975010150 for overnight watch. Leaving notes below: 
- mitigation: prefix reuse disabled in eu-west-1/us-east-1
- flush: shards 11-14 flushed of gpt* keys
- affected customers: AcmeCorp (P1), PixelPay (P2), LibratoAI (P3)
- next steps: revert normalization, backfill safe keys, add linting
sanjay: Acknowledged. I'll take over on-call. Please DM me traces for AcmeCorp flows.
kevin: Sending trace bundle to sanjay: link: https://s3.redwood/traces/incident1975009876/trace-bundle.tar.gz
aisha: CSM pinged AcmeCorp: CSM flagged they saw increased hallucinations and are asking for ETA. We should include ETA in customer note: ETA for mitigation completion: 2-4 hours for full revert deploy and backfill.
marta: PR approved, targeting hotfix deploy in next 90 minutes.
irene: Status update for status.redwood.com: "Investigating: routing cache key normalization bug causing wrong model variants to be served to a subset of customers in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. Mitigation in place: prefix reuse temporarily disabled and caches flushed. Hotfix in progress."
support-bot: Posted to status.redwood.com and created support ticket links for affected customers. Ticket IDs: S-1975-Acme, S-1975-Pixel, S-1975-Librato.
kevin: Monitoring: error rates returning to baseline. No new reports from other regions yet.
aisha: Postmortem owner: marta. Target window for full postmortem draft: 72 hours.
irene: Closing loop: if error rates remain low for next 30m and customer feedback is quiet, we can transition to monitoring-only and finalize mitigation tasks.
sanjay: I'll keep watch and escalate if we see regressions.
opsbot: Incident resolved (mitigation live, follow-up required) at 1975009958 :white_check_mark:
